title: Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana: Rs 2 Lakh Grant, Apply Online
meta_description: Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana: Rs 2 lakh grant with no repayment for poor Bihar families. Apply at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. All castes eligible, 62 business types.

hero.one_liner: Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana gives poor families a Rs 2 lakh business grant with no repayment. Apply at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. All castes, 62 business types.

what_is_it: The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana is a scheme by the Bihar government that provides a one-time business grant of Rs 2 lakh to poor families across all castes to set up a small enterprise. Unlike most business schemes that offer subsidised loans, this scheme gives the Rs 2 lakh as a non-repayable grant — the beneficiary keeps the money and does not pay it back.

The scheme is managed through the official portal at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in, where all applications are submitted and processed. The portal also shows application status at every stage, from document verification through instalment disbursement.

eligibility.label: Selection
eligibility.value: By computer lottery, not first-come. Eligibility is checked, then names are drawn.

eligibility.value: Permanent Bihar resident, generally aged 18 to 50.

eligibility_filters.notes: Bihar families with monthly income under Rs 6,000 (from the Caste Survey). Rs 2 lakh grant, no repayment, no collateral, no education or caste bar. Generally aged 18-50, one per family, not already on Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana. Selection is by computer lottery. Apply at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in.

how_to_apply.title: Register on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in with Aadhaar OTP
how_to_apply.description: Visit the official portal at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in and click on 'Apply Now' or 'Avedan Karen'. Complete Aadhaar-based registration by entering your 12-digit Aadhaar number and verifying with the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. This registration links your application uniquely to your Aadhaar and enables DBT payment to your bank account.

how_to_apply.title: Fill in the application form and select your business category
how_to_apply.description: After registration, fill in your personal details, Bihar address, family income, nominee details, and bank account information. Select one of the 62 approved business categories that you plan to start. Write a brief description of your proposed business, including what you will make or sell, who your customers will be, and what inputs or equipment you need to buy with the grant.

how_to_apply.title: Upload required documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload scanned copies of your Aadhaar card, a recent passport-size photograph, the income certificate from the revenue department showing family monthly income below Rs 6,000, and a bank passbook copy showing your account number and IFSC. The income certificate is the most critical document and must be current, typically issued within the last six months.

how_to_apply.title: Submit and note your application reference number
how_to_apply.description: Review all details carefully and submit the application on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. The portal generates an application reference number after successful submission. Save this number for tracking your status, receiving training schedule alerts, and coordinating with the District Industries Centre (DIC) about verification visits and instalment processing.

how_to_apply.title: Attend mandatory business training and receive the second instalment
how_to_apply.description: After your application is verified and the first instalment of Rs 50,000 is credited, you will be scheduled for business training arranged by the DIC. Attend all required sessions covering business operations, bookkeeping, and trade-specific skills. After training completion is confirmed, the second instalment of Rs 1,00,000 is released to your bank account.

how_to_apply.title: Set up the business and receive the final instalment
how_to_apply.description: Use the first two instalments (Rs 1,50,000 total) to set up your business as described in your application. A DIC field officer will visit to verify that the business is operational. After the inspection confirms your business is running, the third instalment of Rs 50,000 is released, completing the full Rs 2 lakh grant. No repayment is ever required.

extra_sections.heading: What Is Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana
content: The primary eligibility condition is family income: the applicant's family monthly income must be less than Rs 6,000. This threshold ensures the scheme targets genuinely poor families rather than those already running established businesses.

Unlike most government business schemes, the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana does not require any minimum educational qualification. A person who has not completed formal schooling can still apply and receive the Rs 2 lakh grant, making it one of the most accessible enterprise schemes in Bihar.

The scheme is open to all castes and communities in Bihar, with no restriction based on caste category, gender, or religion. Both men and women from any social background can apply, provided the income and residency criteria are met.

The scheme covers 62 types of businesses across five broad sectors: manufacturing, service, trade, construction, and food processing. Applicants must select one of these 62 approved categories at the time of application.

Applicants should nominate the correct bank account at the time of application for DBT payments. If account details change after submission, the update must be made through laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in before the next instalment is processed, as payments to incorrect accounts cause delays and require re-initiation.

The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana does not require prior business experience from the applicant. The mandatory DIC training programme is specifically designed to give first-time entrepreneurs the foundational knowledge needed to run their selected business successfully.

After completing training and setting up the business, beneficiaries who wish to expand beyond the Rs 2 lakh foundation can explore PM Mudra loans. The Shishu tier offers up to Rs 50,000 and the Kishore tier up to Rs 5 lakh for micro-businesses with a track record.

extra_sections.title: Selection Is by Lottery, Not First-Come
extra_sections.content:
Applying does not guarantee the grant. Eligible applications go into a computer lottery, and names are drawn at random. Marks, education, and application speed do not matter.

So apply within the window, but understand that selection is a draw. If not selected in one round, you can apply again in the next.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The training provided under the scheme is calibrated to the selected business type and covers basic operations, bookkeeping, and trade-specific skills.

The business training is arranged through District Industries Centres (DICs) and other implementing agencies. Training covers basic business operations, bookkeeping, and skills specific to the chosen business category.
Completion of this training is mandatory before the second instalment of Rs 1,00,000 is released to the beneficiary's bank account.

Applicants must be permanent residents of Bihar and above 18 years of age. They must not already be availing benefits from a similar enterprise promotion scheme run by the central or state government.

The Bihar government opened application windows on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in in phased rollouts, with lakhs of families targeted for coverage across the state. Eligible families should apply during open windows rather than waiting, as processing time is longer when application volumes are high.

extra_sections.heading: The Rs 6,000 Income Rule
content: This restriction ensures the Rs 2 lakh reaches genuinely first-time enterprise entrants from poor families, not those who have already received start-up support.

The application process on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in requires Aadhaar-based registration. The applicant's Aadhaar must be linked to their bank account because the Rs 2 lakh is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
No physical cash disbursement is made under this scheme; all three instalments go directly to the applicant's bank account via DBT.

The income certificate for the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana must be issued by the competent revenue authority, typically the Circle Officer or Tehsildar. Certificates from unofficial sources or private notaries are not accepted under this scheme.

Applicants should keep a copy of their application acknowledgment number after submission. This number is needed to track status on the portal, coordinate with the DIC about training schedules, and receive communication about inspection visits and instalment release dates.

extra_sections.heading: How the Rs 2 Lakh Is Released
content: The certificate must specifically state that the family's monthly income is below Rs 6,000 and must be current, typically not older than six months at the time of application.

Applicants should check their application status on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in after submitting. The portal shows whether the application is under review, approved, scheduled for training, or awaiting field inspection.
Applicants should also watch for SMS notifications on their Aadhaar-linked mobile number, which is sent at each key stage of the disbursement process.

Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana must be clearly distinguished from the Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana, which is a separate scheme at udyami.bihar.gov.in that offers Rs 10 lakh and is restricted to SC, ST, EBC, and women applicants who have passed Class 12. The Laghu Udyami scheme offers Rs 2 lakh as a full grant, is open to all categories, and has no education bar.

The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana is distinct from the PM Vishwakarma scheme, which targets traditional artisans in specific hereditary trades. The Laghu Udyami scheme is broader, covering any of the 62 approved categories and open to all Bihar families with income below Rs 6,000 per month, regardless of traditional occupation.

extra_sections.title: How the Grant Is Paid
extra_sections.content:
The Rs 2 lakh is paid through DBT to your bank account, with mandatory DIC business training between stages. The release structure has been revised over time.

It has historically been paid in instalments tied to training and setup. Confirm the current instalment structure on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in before you plan your spending.

extra_sections.heading: The 62 Business Types
content: The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana benefit is one-time per family. A family that has already received the Rs 2 lakh grant cannot apply again for the same scheme, as the intent is to reach the maximum number of unserved families across Bihar.

Manufacturing businesses under the scheme include a wide range of home-based and workshop activities. Garment stitching, bamboo and cane products, incense stick manufacturing, soap and candle making, leather goods, and handloom weaving are among the manufacturing categories covered.

Service sector businesses are among the most popular choices under the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana. Mobile phone repair, two-wheeler servicing, electrical appliance repair, beauty parlour, photography, tailoring, and computer repair can all be started with the Rs 2 lakh grant.

Food processing businesses are particularly suitable for rural Bihar, where agricultural produce is available locally. Pickle making, papad manufacturing, flour milling, bakery operations, juice making, and dairy product processing are food processing options covered under the scheme.

Trade or retail businesses covered under the scheme include kirana stores, vegetable and fruit vending, cloth retail, hardware shops, and dairy product shops. These can be started with modest infrastructure and generate steady daily income from local customers in both urban and rural areas.

extra_sections.title: Across Five Broad Sectors
extra_sections.desc:
The scheme covers 62 business types across manufacturing, service, trade, construction, and agriculture-linked sectors.

Popular choices include tailoring, beauty parlours, mobile repair, flour mills, food processing, and furniture making. You choose one type when you apply.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply Online
content: Women applicants are particularly encouraged under the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana. The scheme makes no distinction between male and female applicants, and the income and residency criteria apply equally to both.
Women planning to start home-based manufacturing, beauty services, tailoring, or food processing businesses are well-suited to benefit from this grant.

Self-help group (SHG) members in Bihar can apply individually for the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana. The scheme's per-family grant is separate from any credit or grants received by the SHG collectively, and SHG membership is not a requirement for eligibility.

The scheme covers both urban and rural applicants with no restriction based on place of residence. Rural applicants in agriculture-adjacent sectors like food processing, dairy, and agricultural tool repair are particularly well-positioned to use the grant productively.

Construction-related businesses covered under the scheme include masonry contracting, plumbing services, electrical contracting for small projects, and painting and finishing work. Workers who already have these practical skills can use the Rs 2 lakh grant to formalise their operation and take on larger contracts.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and the Income Certificate
content: SC and ST applicants who are eligible for both the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana and the Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana must choose which scheme to apply under. Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana offers more capital (Rs 10 lakh) for those who need larger investment, while Laghu Udyami is better for very simple micro-businesses with lower start-up costs.

The District Industries Centre (DIC) plays a key role in implementing the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana. DICs verify applications, arrange training programmes, conduct field inspections, and maintain beneficiary records in each district.
Applicants who need assistance with the online process can approach their nearest DIC for guided support or visit a Common Service Centre (CSC) for assisted registration on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in.

Beneficiaries who receive the Rs 2 lakh grant should use a separate bank account for managing the grant funds. Mixing personal and business funds can create difficulty during the field verification inspection before the third instalment.

The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana application must include a proposed business description aligned with the chosen category. Selecting a business type and then describing a completely different activity in the description can lead to application rejection during DIC verification.

extra_sections.heading: Training and DIC Support
content: A dedicated business account also helps the beneficiary build a formal banking record, which is useful for accessing credit from banks under PM Mudra or other MSME schemes after the business is running.

The Bihar state government funds the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana entirely from the state budget. Unlike centrally sponsored schemes that require beneficiaries to contribute margin money, the Rs 2 lakh here is fully government-funded with no personal capital contribution required from the applicant.

The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana encourages linkages with the Kushal Yuva Programme (KYP), Bihar's state-level skill training initiative. Young applicants who have completed KYP training in relevant trades arrive with formal skills that complement the start-up grant and improve business success rates.
The grant amount of Rs 2 lakh is calibrated to typical micro-enterprise start-up costs. A mason starting a contracting business can purchase tools and safety equipment.

Migrant workers who have returned to Bihar and wish to restart their livelihoods are eligible for the scheme, provided they meet the income threshold and residency requirements. Return migrants with construction, garment, or repair skills can use the grant to set up a similar enterprise in their home district.

extra_sections.text: A woman from a poor family in Muzaffarpur earning Rs 5,000 a month can apply for the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. She does not need a class 10 certificate, a guarantor, or collateral. She can choose to start a pickle-making business or a beauty parlour. The Rs 2 lakh comes in three instalments as she sets up her business. She never repays it.

extra_sections.heading: Distinct From Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana
content: A woman starting a beauty parlour can buy salon furniture, equipment, and an initial stock of cosmetics with the Rs 2 lakh grant.

After the business is established and generating income, beneficiaries are encouraged to apply for Udyam registration through udyamregistration.gov.in. Formal Udyam registration opens access to MSME benefits including priority sector lending, GST exemptions on small turnover, and government procurement participation.

Once the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana business is operational, the beneficiary can also approach banks for additional credit under PM Mudra's Shishu (Rs 50,000) or Kishore (Rs 5 lakh) tiers. An operational business with Udyam registration serves as a credibility anchor for the bank's credit assessment.

If a beneficiary faces genuine hardship after receiving the first two instalments and cannot set up the business as planned due to health or family circumstances, they should contact their DIC office. The DIC has discretion to grant extended timelines for the field inspection before the third instalment is released.

Each district in Bihar has a designated target number of beneficiaries under the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana. These targets are distributed across blocks and panchayats to ensure the scheme reaches rural and semi-urban areas, not just district headquarters.

extra_sections.heading: Practical Tips and Process
content: Workers in brick kilns, stone quarries, and local construction in rural Bihar can use the grant to transition from daily wage work to running a small contracting enterprise. Owning professional tools and a working capital reserve is often sufficient to move from worker to petty contractor in rural markets.

Applicants who are not comfortable with online portals can visit a nearby Common Service Centre (CSC) or Jan Seva Kendra for assisted application on laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. CSC operators charge a small service fee for assistance, which is not part of the government scheme cost.

The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana is part of Bihar's broader strategy to reduce poverty and unemployment by encouraging micro-entrepreneurship at the family level. By removing educational barriers and covering all castes and communities, the scheme is designed to have the widest possible reach across Bihar's diverse population.

faqs.question: What is the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana (Mukhyamantri Laghu Udyami Yojana) is a Bihar state government scheme that gives a Rs 2 lakh one-time business grant to poor families with monthly income below Rs 6,000. The grant is not a loan and does not need to be repaid. It is open to all castes, has no education requirement, and covers 62 business types. Applications are made at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: Eligibility: Bihar resident, age 18+, family monthly income below Rs 6,000, no previous benefit from a similar government enterprise scheme. No minimum education qualification is required. The scheme is open to all castes and communities including General, OBC, SC, ST, and EBC. Both men and women can apply.

faqs.question: How much grant is given under Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The grant is Rs 2 lakh per family, released in three instalments via DBT. First instalment: Rs 50,000 after application approval. Second instalment: Rs 1,00,000 after completing mandatory business training. Third instalment: Rs 50,000 after field verification confirms the business is operational. The full amount is a grant with no repayment.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: Apply online at laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. Register using Aadhaar OTP, fill in the application form, select one of the 62 approved business categories, upload documents (Aadhaar, income certificate below Rs 6,000/month, bank passbook, photo), and submit. Save your application reference number for tracking status and DIC coordination.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: Required documents: Aadhaar card, passport-size photograph, income certificate from the revenue department (Circle Officer or Tehsildar) confirming family monthly income below Rs 6,000, and bank passbook copy with account number and IFSC. No caste certificate is needed as the scheme is open to all categories. No education certificate is required.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana and Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: These are two separate schemes. Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana: Rs 2 lakh full grant (no repayment), all categories, no education requirement, portal laghuudyami.bihar.gov.in. Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana: Rs 10 lakh (50% subsidy + 50% repayable loan), restricted to SC/ST/EBC/Women, requires Class 12 pass, portal udyami.bihar.gov.in. Do not confuse the two.

faqs.question: Which businesses can I start under Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers 62 approved business categories across 5 sectors. Manufacturing: garment stitching, soap making, candles, bamboo products, furniture. Service: mobile repair, beauty parlour, tailoring, two-wheeler servicing. Trade: kirana store, vegetable vending, cloth shop. Construction: masonry, plumbing, painting. Food processing: pickle, papad, flour mill, bakery, dairy. You must select one category at the time of application.

faqs.question: Is Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana a loan or a grant?
faqs.answer: It is a grant, not a loan. The Rs 2 lakh given under the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana does not need to be repaid. There is no interest, no EMI, no repayment schedule, and no collateral. This is the key feature that distinguishes this scheme from subsidised loan programmes like PM Mudra or Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana.

faqs.question: How is the Rs 2 lakh released under Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The Rs 2 lakh is released in 3 instalments via DBT. Instalment 1 (Rs 50,000): after application approval and DIC document verification. Instalment 2 (Rs 1,00,000): after completing mandatory business training arranged by the DIC. Instalment 3 (Rs 50,000): after a DIC field officer inspects and confirms the business is operational.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The family monthly income must be less than Rs 6,000. This is verified through a current income certificate issued by the revenue department (Circle Officer or Tehsildar). The certificate must specifically state the family income is below Rs 6,000 per month and should not be older than six months at the time of application.
